mainTopic: When intent to eat makes a kosher bird's carcass or produce impure: intent during life or while attached, the chicken of יבנה, and the bird in the winepress
overview: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling that intent while produce is still attached to the ground does not count. רבא supports this from a משנה that a kosher bird's carcass needs intent, so intent while it was alive must not count either. רבי זירא pushes back: the משנה may be about a bird nobody saw alive. He explains the chicken of יבנה as a 'wild' chicken, which אביי says means a kosher chick born to a runaway hen. רב פפא says instead that it was a marsh hen, which he holds is kosher, while מרימר says the marsh hen is forbidden. Next comes a ברייתא about a young bird that fell into a winepress: if the owner planned it for a כותי it is impure, and if for a dog it is pure. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says it is impure even for a dog, using a קל וחומר, and the חכמים reject his argument. The גמרא places the case in a big city where the winepress made the bird disgusting, and רבא begins explaining the חכמים's reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: intent counts only after picking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that these items need intent to be food once they are picked. His reason is that intent while they are still attached to the ground does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need intent once they are picked. He holds that intent while they are still attached is not considered intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יוחנן's ruling and gives the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can become susceptible to food טומאה only if a person treats it as food, through מחשבה. רבי יוחנן says that thinking about the produce while it is still growing in the ground does not do the job. So the person must have intent again after picking it.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent, a person's decision to treat something as food
Once they are picked (detached from the ground)
Intent formed while the produce is still attached to the ground
He holds, introducing the reasoning behind a ruling

phrases.english: they require intent once they are detached,
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of רבי יוחנן's ruling from just before. 'They' means the produce being discussed there.

phrases.english: he holds that intent while attached

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר מַחְשֶׁבֶת חִבּוּר לֹא שְׁמָהּ מַחְשָׁבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ruling of רבי יוחנן that was begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent formed while produce is still attached to the ground does not count, so new intent is needed after picking.

steps.title: רבא's support from the kosher bird carcass
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה: the carcass of a kosher bird needs intent but does not need הכשר. He learns from this that intent while the bird was alive does not count, and the same is true of intent while produce is attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We also learned this. Thirteen things were said about the carcass of a kosher bird, and this is one of them: it needs intent, but it does not need to be made susceptible by liquid. So intent while it was alive is not called intent. Here too, intent while attached is not called intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports רבי יוחנן with a משנה about נבלת עוף טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the bird's carcass needs intent, even though people normally plan to eat a kosher bird while it is alive. If intent during life counted, the carcass would not need new intent. So intent during life must not count, and רבא compares this to intent while produce is attached to the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a kosher bird that died without proper שחיטה
Making food susceptible to טומאה by wetting it with liquid
Intent formed while the animal is still alive
Evidently, we see from here
We also learned this, introducing support from a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse מחשבה with הכשר. מחשבה means deciding that something is food. הכשר means it got wet with a liquid. The bird carcass needs the first but not the second.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned this,
phrases.notes: The source is the משנה in טהרות 1:1.

phrases.english: regarding the carcass of a kosher bird,
and this is one of them:
but does not require being rendered susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of step 1 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's principle that intent before something is ready, while attached, does not count.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה טהרות 1:1: a kosher bird carcass requires intent, which shows that intent during the bird's life does not count.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the bird fell from a height
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rejects the proof. The משנה may be about a young bird that fell from a height, so no one had it in front of them to have intent while it was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Here we are dealing with a young bird that fell from a height, which was not in front of us so that we could have intent about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back on רבא's proof by reading the משנה as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי זירא's case, nobody ever had intent while the bird was alive. That is why intent is needed after it dies. So the משנה does not prove that intent during life fails to count, and it might count when someone actually had it.

keyTerms.meaning: A young bird, a chick
A height, a high place
We are dealing with, setting up a specific case
Before us, in our presence

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּגוֹזָל שֶׁנָּפַל מִן הָרוּם עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: here we are dealing with a young bird that fell from a height,
so that we could have intent about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּגוֹזָל שֶׁנָּפַל מִן הָרוּם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 2 by limiting the משנה to a case with no intent during the bird's life.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבי יוחנן's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה could describe a bird that no one had intent about while it was alive, so it says nothing about whether such intent would count.

steps.title: אביי challenges with the chicken in Yavne
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבי זירא how he would explain the case of the chicken in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is there to say about the chicken in Yavne?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי זירא's answer with a known case, the chicken in יבנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יבנה case, the chicken needed intent after it died, even though it seems people had it in front of them while it was alive. That suggests intent during life does not count, which is רבא's point. It does not fit רבי זירא's 'nobody saw it' explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A hen, a chicken
יבנה, the town where the חכמים gathered
What is there to say? A challenge asking how a case can be explained

phrases.notes: This refers to a known case where the חכמים ruled that the chicken became impure through intent only after it was already a carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת שֶׁבְּיַבְנֶה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's explanation in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that intent is needed afterward only when no one saw the bird alive.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In יבנה the chicken seems to have been in front of people while alive, yet it still needed intent after death. That suggests intent during life does not count.

steps.title: רבי זירא: it was a wild chicken
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the יבנה chicken was a wild chicken, so no one had it in front of them while it was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was a wild chicken.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers אביי by saying the יבנה chicken was a wild one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wild chicken was not kept by people, so nobody had intent about it while it was alive. That makes the יבנה case just like the young bird that fell from a height, and רבי זירא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild chicken, not a domestic one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and רבא hold that intent formed before something is ready, while attached or alive, does not count. רבי זירא avoids the proof by explaining that the bird cases are ones where no intent ever happened during life.
steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְנְגוֹל בָּרָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 4 and defends step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the chicken was wild, not domestic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבנה chicken was a domestic bird that people had in front of them while it was alive, so intent during life failed to count.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a wild chicken that no one had in front of them while it was alive, so it fits רבי זירא's explanation.

steps.title: The listeners laugh: a wild chicken is not even kosher
steps.stepSummary: People laugh at רבי זירא's answer. A wild chicken is an עוף טמא, and a non-kosher bird's carcass does not make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him: A wild chicken is a non-kosher bird, and does a non-kosher bird make things impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The listeners attack רבי זירא's answer from Step 5. They say a wild chicken is not kosher, so it could never be the impure carcass in the יבנה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבנה case is about the carcass of a kosher bird, which can become impure. If the יבנה chicken were a non-kosher bird, there would be no impurity to discuss. So רבי זירא's answer seems to wipe out the whole case.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at him
A wild (outdoor) chicken
A non-kosher bird

phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי זירא, who just said the יבנה chicken was a wild chicken.

phrases.english: A wild chicken is a non-kosher bird,
and does a non-kosher bird make things impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the יבנה chicken was a תרנגול ברא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wild chicken is non-kosher, so its carcass cannot carry the impurity the case is about.

steps.title: אביי defends him: a chicken born to a runaway hen
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells them not to laugh at a great man. רבי זירא meant a kosher chicken whose mother ran away, so it was born out in the wild.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: A great man said something, do not laugh at him. He meant a hen that rebelled. And what does "wild" mean? That it was created from the rebel one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי זירא. The chicken was a normal kosher chicken. It was simply born in the wild to a hen that had run away from her owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בָּרָא does not mean a non-kosher wild species. It means a kosher chicken that came from a hen that escaped. Since it grew up in the wild, no one had it in front of them while it was alive, so no one could have had intent then.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man
A hen that rebelled, meaning it ran away from its owner
That was created, or born

phrases.english: he meant a hen that rebelled,
That it was created from the rebel one.
phrases.notes: A play on words: בָּרָא, "wild," sounds like אִיבְּרַאי, "was created." The chick came from the hen that ran away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה אֲמַר מִילְּתָא, לָא תְּחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by reading רבי זירא's word differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בָּרָא means a wild, non-kosher species.
steps.terutzMaskana: בָּרָא means a kosher chicken born to a hen that ran away. It is kosher, but no one had it in front of them while it was alive.

steps.title: רב פפא: it was a marsh hen
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different explanation of the יבנה chicken. It was a hen that lives in the marshes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It was a marsh hen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers another way to explain the יבנה case. The bird was a kosher marsh hen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A marsh hen lives where people do not. So no one had it in front of them to have intent while it was alive, and intent was needed after it died. This keeps the bird kosher and avoids the laughter's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A marsh hen
Marsh

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא דְּאַגְמָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, alongside אביי's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבנה chicken was a non-kosher wild bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a kosher marsh hen that no one had in front of them while it was alive.

steps.title: רב פפא is consistent: marsh hen kosher, marsh rooster not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב פפא follows his own known ruling: the marsh rooster is forbidden and the marsh hen is permitted. It gives a memory aid: עמוני ולא עמונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא follows his own reasoning, as רב פפא said: The marsh rooster is forbidden, the marsh hen is permitted. And your memory aid: "An Ammonite man and not an Ammonite woman."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא's answer. It points to another ruling of his showing he holds the marsh hen is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer only works if the marsh hen is kosher. His separate ruling shows he holds exactly that. The memory aid helps you remember: as with עמוני and עמונית, the male is forbidden and the female is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning
Forbidden / permitted
And your memory aid
An Ammonite man may not marry into the Jewish people, but an Ammonite woman may

phrases.english: רב פפא follows his own reasoning,
"An Ammonite man and not an Ammonite woman."
phrases.notes: Just like there, the male one is forbidden and the female one is allowed. דברים 23:4

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's answer by pointing to his own ruling elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: That רב פפא holds the marsh hen is a kosher bird
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא's ruling: the marsh rooster is forbidden and the marsh hen is permitted

steps.title: מרימר: the marsh hen is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: מרימר taught that the marsh hen is forbidden. The rabbis saw it attack and eat prey, and it is the bird called גירותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: The marsh hen is forbidden. The rabbis saw that it attacked and ate its prey, and this is the גירותא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that disagrees with רב פפא. According to מרימר, the marsh hen is not kosher at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרימר bases his ruling on what the rabbis saw: the bird attacks and eats prey, which is a sign of a non-kosher bird. He also identifies it as the bird known as גירותא. This goes against רב פפא's ruling that the marsh hen is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught in a public lecture
That it attacks (claws) its prey
The name of a non-kosher bird

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רב פפא says the marsh hen is kosher. מרימר says it is forbidden.

phrases.english: that it attacked and ate its prey,

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ מָרִימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that disagrees with רב פפא's ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The marsh hen is forbidden, since it attacks and eats prey. It is the גירותא.

steps.title: A young bird in a winepress: the plan decides
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a young bird fell into a winepress and died. If the owner planned to take it out for a כותי, it is impure. If he planned it for a dog, it is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: A young bird that fell into a winepress, and the owner planned to take it out for a כותי, is impure. If he planned it for a dog, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a young bird that fell and died, much like the bird in Step 3. Here the owner's plan for the dead bird decides its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plan to give the bird to a person (a כותי) counts as intent to treat it as food, so it becomes impure. A plan to give it to a dog is not intent for human food, so it stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A young bird
Winepress
He intended, or planned
A Samaritan

phrases.english: A young bird that fell into a winepress,
and he planned to take it out
for a כותי: it is impure,
phrases.notes: A כותי is a person who would eat it, so this counts as planning it as food.

phrases.english: for a dog: it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גּוֹזָל שֶׁנָּפַל לַגַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about a young bird that fell, connected to the young bird case in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planning the dead bird for a person makes it impure. Planning it for a dog leaves it pure.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: even for a dog it is impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees: even if the owner planned the bird for a dog, it is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: Even for a dog, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא disagrees with the first ruling about the dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion, only a plan for human food makes the bird impure. רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds it is impure even with a plan for a dog. In his view, the carcass of a kosher bird does not need a plan to be food at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Impure / pure

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion: a plan to feed the bird to a person (a כותי) makes it impure, but a plan to feed it to a dog does not. רבי יוחנן בן נורי: even a plan to feed it to a dog leaves it impure.

phrases.english: Even for a dog, it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אַף לְכֶלֶב טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's ruling about the dog in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird is impure even when the owner planned it for a dog.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי proves his view with a קל וחומר. The kosher bird carcass gives severe impurity without intent, so it should give the lighter food impurity without intent too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: Here is a קל וחומר. If this carcass gives severe impurity even when nobody intended it for eating, shouldn't it also give the lighter impurity without intent?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי explains why he says the bird is impure even if the owner planned it for a dog. He uses a 'how much more so' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher bird's carcass already gives severe impurity with no intent needed. He reasons that the lighter food impurity should surely work without intent too. If he is right, the owner's plan for the bird (כותי or dog) should not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from lighter to stricter: if a rule applies in the weaker case, it surely applies in the stronger one.
Severe impurity. Here it means the kosher bird carcass making a person's clothes impure when it is swallowed.
Lighter impurity. Here it means ordinary food impurity, passed on by touch.
Intent. Here it means planning that the item be eaten by a person.

phrases.english: It is a 'how much more so' argument:

phrases.notes: 'It' is the kosher bird's carcass. Its severe impurity makes your clothes impure when you swallow it.

phrases.english: should it not transmit lighter impurity

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The bird is impure as food even without intent, even if the owner planned it for a dog.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the severe impurity of a kosher bird carcass, which needs no intent.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the קל וחומר fails. Severe impurity has nothing to do with intent, but lighter food impurity is exactly the kind where intent matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No! You can say that about severe impurity, because intent plays no part in it. But can you say it about lighter impurity, where intent does play a part?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים knock down the קל וחומר. They point out a difference between the two kinds of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the two cases are alike in what counts. The חכמים say intent simply doesn't apply to severe impurity, so it proves nothing about food impurity, where intent does apply. The גמרא asks what 'comes into that' means in step 23, and רבא starts explaining it in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No, if you said...' The standard way to reject a קל וחומר by showing a difference.
Literally 'goes down to this.' It means this kind of impurity is one where intent plays a part.

phrases.english: If you said this about severe impurity,
that is because it does not come into that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means the system of intent. The גמרא asks about this phrase in step 23.

phrases.english: will you say it about lighter impurity,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּטוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two kinds of impurity are not alike. Intent is irrelevant to severe impurity but relevant to food impurity.

steps.title: The chicken of יבנה as a counter-proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי points to the chicken of יבנה. It was the kind of case where intent matters, yet it was declared impure without intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The chicken of יבנה proves my point. It was the kind where intent matters, and still they declared it impure without intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers the חכמים with a real case. He shows that even lighter impurity worked without intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said food impurity needs intent. He brings an actual ruling, the יבנה chicken (the case אביי raised in step 4), where food impurity applied with no intent. This would show the חכמים' difference does not matter in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove.' Bringing a known case to show your point.
'They declared it impure.'

phrases.english: The chicken in יבנה will prove it,
and yet they declared it impure without intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת שֶׁבְּיַבְנֶה תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' rejection in step 14 with an actual case.
steps.raayaObject: Food impurity can apply to a kosher bird carcass without intent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling about the chicken of יבנה.

steps.title: The חכמים: in יבנה there was intent
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the יבנה proof. There were כותים in יבנה, so people did intend the chicken for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof? There were כותים there, and people intended it to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back the proof from the יבנה chicken. They say intent really was present there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the יבנה chicken became impure with no intent. The חכמים say there were כותים in town who would eat it, so people did plan it for eating. The case fits their own view after all, so the debate stays where it was.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is there proof from there?' A way of saying the case does not prove anything.
Samaritans. Here, people in the area who would eat such a bird.
'For eating.'

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there proof from there?
and they intended it for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the יבנה chicken in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the יבנה chicken only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There was intent in יבנה, because כותים were there to eat it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says intent is not needed (קל וחומר and the יבנה chicken). The חכמים answer that food impurity does depend on intent, and in יבנה there was intent because of the כותים.

steps.title: What setting is the winepress case in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא of the bird in the winepress and asks what kind of place it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what kind of place the winepress ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether intent is needed may depend on where the bird is found. So the גמרא wants to pin down the setting of the case from step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are we dealing with?' Asks for the exact case or setting.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the young bird that fell into the winepress (step 11).

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate and goes back to analyze the ברייתא from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The setting of the winepress case: a big city or another kind of place.

steps.title: Not big cities, where no intent is needed
steps.stepSummary: The case can't be in big cities. A משנה says a kosher bird's carcass in big cities needs no intent at all, yet the ברייתא makes intent matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it's in big cities, why does it need intent? But we learned in a משנה: the carcass of a kosher animal anywhere, and the carcass of a kosher bird and forbidden fat in big cities, need neither intent nor הכשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, big cities, and rejects it at once. A משנה says such carcasses in big cities need no intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the owner's plan (כותי or dog) decides whether the bird is impure, so intent matters there. The משנה says a kosher bird carcass in big cities needs neither intent nor הכשר. So the ברייתא can't be about big cities, and the גמרא must look for another setting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say.' Introduces a possible answer that the גמרא is about to test.
Big cities. Places with many people.
A carcass of an animal or bird that was not properly slaughtered.
Getting wet, which makes food able to become impure.
Forbidden fat of an animal.

phrases.english: If you say it is in big cities,
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The carcass of a kosher animal, in any place,
and the carcass of a kosher bird and the forbidden fat, in big cities,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צְרִיכִין לֹא מַחְשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בִּכְרַכִּים, לְמָה לַהּ מַחְשָׁבָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible setting for the question in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the winepress ברייתא (step 11) as a case in big cities.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In big cities a kosher bird carcass needs no intent, according to the משנה. But the ברייתא makes the owner's intent decide the outcome, so it can't be about big cities.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the ברייתא is wrong. It is only ruling out one possible setting (big cities) so it can find the right one.

steps.title: Villages don't work either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries placing the ברייתא in villages. It rejects this, because a משנה says a kosher bird's carcass in villages definitely needs intent, so nobody could say it doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about villages. But is there anyone who says intent is not needed there? Didn't we learn in a משנה: a carcass of a non-kosher animal anywhere, and a carcass of a kosher bird in villages, need intent but do not need to be made susceptible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about villages, then immediately shows this fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds the bird is impure even without intent. But the משנה clearly says a kosher bird's carcass in a village needs intent, with no argument recorded. So placing the case in villages would leave רבי יוחנן בן נורי arguing against a plain משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Villages, small places with few people who might eat such a carcass
Intent, here meaning a plan to use the carcass as food
Being made susceptible to impurity by contact with a liquid
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not slaughtered properly
The carcass of a non-kosher animal

steps.confusionAlert: Both big cities (Step 18) and villages (this step) are ruled out for opposite reasons. In big cities nobody needs intent, and in villages everybody needs intent. The ברייתא has an argument, so it needs a case where intent is really in question.

phrases.english: Rather, it is talking about villages.
But is there anyone who says

phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who in the ברייתא says the bird is impure without intent.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The carcass of a non-kosher animal, in any place,
and the carcass of a kosher bird in villages
but do not require being made susceptible!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא מַחְשָׁבָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After big cities failed in Step 18, this tries the other option, villages, and knocks it down too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the ברייתא is about villages
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules without dispute that a kosher bird's carcass in villages needs intent, so רבי יוחנן בן נורי could not hold that no intent is needed there.

steps.title: A big city, but the winepress made the bird disgusting
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא בר חנינא says the case is in a big city. Because the bird fell into a winepress and became disgusting, it is treated like a village bird, so intent becomes a real question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא בר חנינא said: Really it is in a big city, but its winepress made it disgusting and made it like a village.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זעירא בר חנינא solves the problem by saying the case is in a big city, with a twist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally in a big city plenty of people would eat a bird carcass, so no intent is needed. Here the bird fell into the winepress and became disgusting, so fewer people would want it. That makes it like a bird in a village, where intent matters, and that is why the חכמים and רבי יוחנן בן נורי can argue about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually, used to keep the first idea and explain it differently
A big, walled city with many people
A winepress
Made it disgusting

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is a big city case, but the winepress made the bird disgusting, so it is treated like a village bird and intent is relevant.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that what counts is how likely people are to eat the item. Location matters only because it changes that, and other things, like the item becoming disgusting, can change it too.

phrases.english: Really, it is in a big city,
but its winepress made it disgusting,
and made it like a village case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: לְעוֹלָם בִּכְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges (Steps 18 and 19) by putting the case in a big city with a special detail.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) with an added detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case had to be either a plain big city, where no intent is needed, or a village, where intent is needed. Neither fits an argument.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a big city, but the winepress made the bird disgusting, so it is like a village bird and intent is a real question.

steps.title: The קל וחומר of רבי יוחנן בן נורי quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the exchange in the ברייתא so it can examine it. It quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר: if the bird carcass gives severe impurity without intent, it should surely give lighter impurity without intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: It is a קל וחומר. If it makes things impure with severe impurity without intent, shouldn't it make things impure with light impurity without intent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי's קל וחומר again so it can look at it more closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher bird's carcass has a severe impurity that needs no intent at all. רבי יוחנן בן נורי argues that the lighter impurity of food should then surely need no intent either. This is the same argument as before. The גמרא brings it again as the starting point for its analysis.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a stricter case to a lighter one: if the strict case has a rule, the light case surely does too
Severe impurity, the strong impurity of a kosher bird's carcass
Light impurity, here the impurity of food

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. The גמרא is repeating the exchange from earlier in the ברייתא (Steps 13 and 14) so it can analyze it.

phrases.english: If it makes things impure with severe impurity
should it not make things impure with light impurity

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is defined, the גמרא returns to the debate inside the ברייתא and quotes it again for analysis.
steps.raayaObject: A kosher bird's carcass imparts food impurity without intent
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from the bird's severe impurity, which needs no intent

steps.title: The חכמים's answer quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים's reply again. Severe impurity is a kind that has nothing to do with intent, so you cannot learn from it to food impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: No. If you said this about severe impurity, that is because it does not come down to this matter of intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes re-quoting the exchange with the חכמים's rejection of the קל וחומר, getting ready to examine their words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say the קל וחומר breaks down. Severe impurity simply has no connection to intent, so its rule tells us nothing about food impurity, where intent is the very thing that matters. The hard words 'אינה יורדת לכך' are what the גמרא asks about in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'it does not go down to this,' meaning intent plays no part in it
Because / since, used to point out how the cases differ

phrases.english: If you said this about severe impurity,
that is because it does not come down to this.
phrases.notes: They mean severe impurity has nothing to do with intent at all, so it can't teach us about food impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּטוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the re-quoted exchange by giving the חכמים's rejection of the קל וחומר from Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר of רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Severe impurity is unrelated to intent, so a rule about it cannot carry over to food impurity, which depends on intent.

steps.title: What does 'it does not assume its status with that' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant by the phrase 'אינה יורדת לכך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it does not assume its status with that' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant when they said the severe impurity 'does not assume its status with that' requirement. It is setting up רבא's explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said severe impurity has nothing to do with intent, so it cannot teach us about food impurity. But the wording is unclear: why would intent matter for the light impurity of a bird carcass and not for the severe impurity it gives in the throat? The גמרא wants the reasoning spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'it does not go down to this.' It means this impurity is not tied to the requirement of intent.
Intent, meaning a person's plan to use something as food.
Severe impurity. Here, the impurity of a kosher bird carcass when it is in the throat, which makes clothes impure.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against the חכמים. The גמרא only wants to understand their words. It is not trying to prove them wrong.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'it does not assume its status with that'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אֵינָהּ יוֹרֶדֶת לְכָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the key phrase in the חכמים's reply quoted in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way is intent unrelated to severe impurity, so that the קל וחומר to food impurity does not work?

steps.title: רבא begins to explain the חכמים's reply
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to reword what the חכמים told רבי יוחנן בן נורי, opening with 'No, if you said...'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what they said to him: No, if you said...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer the question by putting the חכמים's reply in clearer words. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא, אם אמרת' is the standard way to start pushing back on a קל וחומר. It shows that the starting case (severe impurity) has a special feature that the food-impurity case lacks. רבא is about to spell out exactly what that feature is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what they said to him.' It introduces a fuller rewording of someone's words.
'No, if you said...' The standard opening for showing that a קל וחומר does not work.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what they said to him:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים, and 'him' is רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
The sentence is not finished yet. רבא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 23 by rewording the חכמים's reply.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא starts to restate the חכמים's reply as a 'לא, אם אמרת' rejection of the קל וחומר. The full content comes in the continuation.
